description: Dev demo and production-ready system structure connecting a 3D Digital Twin to the existing EIS-ERP, including AI-assisted reflector-based position simulation.

referenceDocuments: D:\DigitalTwin3D\Document\ระบบ AI จำลองตำแหน่งด้วยตัวสะท้อน.pdf
context.priority: Start with a demonstrable local/dev demo, while defining complete service, data, integration, security, and deployment boundaries.

questions.question: Which language should the Digital Twin 3D web application use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Strong typing for 3D scene state, ERP contracts, telemetry, and demo evolution.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Faster minimal setup but less compile-time protection for integration-heavy code.

questions.rationale: The demo needs reliable typed contracts between 3D rendering, AI simulation, and ERP APIs.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and 3D approach should be used?

options.label: React + Three.js/React Three Fiber
options.description: Recommended ecosystem for interactive 3D scenes, panels, and reusable UI.

options.label: Vue + Three.js
options.description: Good component model with a separate Three.js integration.

options.label: Plain TypeScript + Three.js
options.description: Smallest runtime surface for a focused proof of concept.

questions.rationale: React provides a maintainable UI shell while Three.js supports the Digital Twin scene.

questions.question: Describe the minimum Digital Twin 3D demo behavior, including scene navigation, asset layers, live/simulated markers, and ERP actions.
questions.recommendedChoice: Interactive facility scene with selectable assets, marker playback, position confidence/status, and links to ERP records.
questions.answer: Interactive facility scene with selectable assets, marker playback, position confidence/status, and links to ERP records.
questions.rationale: These capabilities demonstrate the end-to-end value without requiring the full production asset inventory.

questions.question: Which language should implement the Digital Twin integration API?

options.label: PHP
options.description: Fits the existing EIS-ERP deployment and allows the demo to reuse current routing and authentication.

options.label: TypeScript (Node.js)
options.description: Suitable for a separate integration service and real-time event processing.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Strong Azure and enterprise integration support for a separately deployed API.

questions.rationale: The current workspace is a PHP/IIS EIS-ERP and a PHP-first demo minimizes integration risk.

questions.question: Which API framework or style should be used for Digital Twin and ERP integration endpoints?

options.label: ASP.NET Core Web API
options.description: Typed, testable API boundary for the Digital Twin and ERP integration.

options.label: Laravel API
options.description: Adds mature conventions but requires a larger application migration boundary.

options.label: Node.js integration service
options.description: Separates real-time integration concerns from the legacy ERP application.

questions.rationale: The demo should first prove connectivity to current ERP modules and database boundaries.

questions.question: Which ERP entities and actions must the first demo integrate (for example assets, locations, supplies, work orders, maintenance, users, and alerts)?
questions.recommendedChoice: Read-only assets/locations plus supplies/work-order deep links, with a controlled simulated-position update endpoint.
questions.answer: items, warehouses, inventory, receiving, picking, and work_orders; read/query flows plus controlled simulation-position updates.
questions.rationale: A read-focused demo is safer while still proving Digital Twin-to-ERP navigation and a traceable position update.

questions.question: Which language should implement the reflector-based position simulation worker?

options.label: Python
options.description: Best fit for numerical simulation, calibration experiments, and future ML integration.

options.label: TypeScript (Node.js)
options.description: Keeps the worker in the web stack but is less convenient for scientific experimentation.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Good enterprise worker option when deployed with the Azure application stack.

questions.rationale: The referenced PDF is about AI-based position simulation using reflectors; Python supports repeatable numerical experiments.

questions.question: Which worker runtime should run repeatable reflector measurements, noise, confidence, and position events?
questions.recommendedChoice: Python worker with a CLI/demo mode and optional FastAPI adapter

options.label: Python worker with a CLI/demo mode and optional FastAPI adapter
options.description: Supports local demos and later queue/API execution without coupling the simulator to the ERP.

options.label: Azure Functions Python
options.description: Useful for event-driven cloud execution but adds Azure storage/runtime requirements early.

options.label: Standalone Python service
options.description: Simple long-running process for development and controlled simulation playback.

questions.rationale: A CLI mode makes the dev demo deterministic; an adapter keeps future deployment options open.

questions.question: Confirm the reflector/AI simulation inputs and outputs, including reflector coordinates, anchor/receiver geometry, sampling rate, noise, calibration, confidence, and replay controls.
questions.recommendedChoice: Deterministic replayable simulation with configurable reflector/receiver geometry, measurement noise, calibration, confidence score, and position event output.
questions.answer: Use the PDF's reflector/receiver, noise, calibration, and confidence parameters with all values adjustable in the UI; emit replayable position events.
questions.rationale: The PDF content must be validated against exact domain parameters during requirements confirmation.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores are required for the dev demo and planned system?

options.label: Microsoft SQL Server
options.description: Existing EIS-ERP relational data, mappings, simulation runs, and audit records.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: 3D assets, scene manifests, uploaded reference files, and generated replay artifacts.

options.label: Redis Cache
options.description: Optional low-latency scene/session and latest-position cache.

options.label: Message Queue
options.description: Optional reliable position-event delivery between simulator, integration API, and UI.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Only for a fully in-memory demo with no ERP persistence or file assets.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The existing ERP uses relational data and the Digital Twin requires 3D/file assets; Blob Storage is also required for an Azure Functions option.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in to access application API features in the dev demo?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Protects Digital Twin views, ERP data, simulation controls, and audit actions.

options.label: No
options.description: Allows an isolated local demo without user sign-in.

sharedQuestions.rationale: ERP-linked data and simulation controls should not be anonymously writable, even in a demo.
